messages:
Maya: Quick sync — Q3 Dedicated commit floor planning for EU/US GPU pools. Need recommended committed GPU counts by EOD tomorrow, who can help with throughput -> GPU conversion?
Alex: I can take a pass. Do we want conservative floors or try to lean on burst credits + on-demand? :thinking_face:
Jon: Share the 95th percentile steady-state RPS per tenant and avg token sizes and I can map to GPUs with our model.
Maya: P95 steady stream (last 30 days): tenant-A 120 rps (avg ~600 tokens), tenant-B 45 rps (avg ~1.2k tokens), tenant-C 30 rps (avg ~4k tokens). These are sustained windows (~10m slices).
Priya: Baseline perf numbers to use: A100-80GB ≈ 1000 tokens/sec/GPU (with our kernel/kv-cache at 512 context). H100 ~= 1.8k tokens/sec/GPU. Tail SLO we keep p99 <= 300ms.
Alex: Rough mapping (quick calc):
```
# rough per-tenant GPU need (no batching)
tenantA_tokens_per_sec = 120 * 600 = 72,000 tps
gpus_for_A = ceil(72000 / 1000) = 72 GPUs (A100)
```
That looks scary but we always get batching + cache benefits.
Jon: 72 looks high because runtime batching and steady coalescing reduce effective load. In practice we see an effective throughput uplift of ~1.8-2x for steady flows.
Priya: If we apply batching factor 2 and prefix/KV caching = 15% reduction: A -> 72k / (1000*2*1.15) ≈ 31 GPUs. B and C scale similarly.
Maya: Okay good. Preliminary ballpark: combined steady need for tenants A+B in eu-west ≈ 40 GPUs after batching+cache. Add headroom for p99 spikes and controller safety.
Alex: Proposal: commit floor = 28 GPUs in eu-west (reserved), plus a 20% burst pool (on-demand or shared reserved slack) to reach 34 w/ margin. Keep the rest as on-demand for occasional H100-backed bursts.
Jon: Two risks: 1) If we undercommit and autoscaler mis-tags instances we get billing mismatches (we saw this in April), 2) cross-tenant noisy neighbor spikes if burst pool is shared.
billing-bot: Billing alert: April invoice flagged ~12% overage for eu-west dedicated pool. Root cause: autoscaler instance tags mis-attributed to commit pool during a deployment. Query created: https://billing.redwood.internal/query/7891 (ticket #7891).
Priya: We should enforce tag immutability during autoscale transitions and add a guard in the allocator to prevent temporary tag flips. I'll draft a quick PR to add tag-enforcement policy.
Maya: For committed sizing across regions: US-west baseline can be 60% of EU-west demand given current tenant geography. So propose us-west reserved = 18 GPUs with same 20% burst cap.
Alex: For cost modeling, Jon — can you run the sim with batching=1.8, cache=15%, and include a conservative 10% extra headroom for replication/maintenance? Need cost delta vs commit sizes {24,28,32}.
Jon: Will run sims and attach the CSV here in ~2 hours. Also will include a sensitivity table for payload changes (+/-25% avg tokens).
Priya: I'll open the autoscaler tag PR and post link. Also adding an integration test that ensures instance->pool tags persist through scale events.
Maya: Action items summarized: Jon -> run final sims + sensitivity and paste results. Alex -> draft commit recommendation per region (numbers + rationale). Priya -> tag enforcement PR + test. Billing-bot -> keep us posted on ticket #7891. Can we have a 30-min call in 30 to align?
Jon: On it. I should have a sim summary in ~2h, can join the call if it's later.
Alex: :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks all — will reconvene after Jon posts sims.
